 This Appeal Coming On For Final Hearing, This
Day, Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:

Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs Justice P Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment

1. A common Judgment was passed by the Principal District and Sessions Judge and MACT,
Raichur, (for short 'the tribunal') in MVC No.332/2021 to MVC No.338/2022 on NC:
2025:KHC-K:6472 HC-KAR 11.12.2023.
It is stated that, out of total seven matters, four matters were settled before the Lok Adalath and the present MFA No.200111/2025 is filed against the award of the tribunal in MVC No.332/2021.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. One Channappa met with accident on 19.04.2021 and succumbed to the injuries.
His wife and children filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.48,00,000/- along with interest.
The tribunal considering the entire evidence on record, awarded a sum of Rs.14,91,168/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Aggrieved by the said Judgment, the claimants have preferred the present appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the claimants/appellants submits that, the deceased was aged 62 years as on the date of the accident and was receiving a sum of Rs.40,671/- as monthly pension.

The tribunal has deducted 25% since the claimant No.1-wife will receive the pension amount and further 50% has been deducted towards personal and living NC: 2025:KHC-K:6472 HC-KAR expenses and loss of consortium is not granted to the children.

Therefore, requests for enhancement of the compensation.
4.

The deceased was working as Senior Assistant (W-E), EE(PS), CE(O&M)T, in the KPCL,
Bengaluru retired from the services after attaining the age of superannuation.
After retirement, he was getting a monthly pension of Rs.40,671/-, as per Ex.P.7 attested copy of the pension payment order.

The tribunal deducted 25% of the pension on the ground that, even after his death, the wife of the deceased will continue to get pension amount, but the said deduction of the tribunal is erroneous and is liable to be set aside.
He was aged 62 years at the time of the accident and the multiplier would be '7'.

He is not entitled for any future prospects and an amount of 1/4th is to be deducted towards personal expenses in view of citation of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130.

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But the tribunal has erred in deducting 50% amount out of the monthly pension.

The loss of dependency would be as under:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6472 HC-KAR Rs.40,671 - 1/4th X 12 X 7 = Rs.25,62,273/-
5.

The claimant No.1 i.e. wife of the deceased is entitled for a sum of Rs.48,000/-
towards loss of consortium and claimant Nos.2 to 4 are entitled for a sum of Rs.48,000/-
each, towards parental consortium in view of citation of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, and

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: all the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- under conventional heads as per the citation of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

Hence, the total compensation would be as under:
Sl.

(iv) Claimant No.1 alone i.e. wife of the deceased is permitted to withdraw the enhanced amount along with interest accrued thereon.
